name: agent-desktop
description: Agent Desktop gives any agent reliable computer use on the desktop. Built with Rust, it sees any app's real UI structure through OS accessibility trees and operates it — refs stay stable and actions stay safe to retry, instead of guessing from pixels.
one_liner: Lets an AI agent actually use the programs on your computer by reading each app's internal UI structure and clicking/typing on it directly, instead of guessing from a screenshot.
buyer: A product team at an RPA or AI-agent startup that needs their agent to reliably operate old desktop software (claims systems, Excel, internal tools) that never got an API.
business_use_cases: An automation agency wires it into back-office bots that process claims inside a 20-year-old desktop insurance system no API was ever built for.
A QA team builds a nightly agent that walks a Windows desktop app end-to-end and files a ticket the moment a step breaks.
An accessibility-testing vendor repurposes the accessibility-tree reader to audit third-party desktop apps for screen-reader compliance.

money_ideas.idea: A hosted desktop-agent API that takes a natural-language instruction and returns verified actions/state for a named app, billed per action.
Paid 'agent-ready' compliance audits for software vendors who want their desktop app certified as reliably automatable.

steal_this: Build a scheduler that logs into one specific painful desktop app (e.g. a dental-practice management tool) every morning, pulls a report, and emails it out — sell that single integration to the many small businesses stuck on that software.
